blocks.text: Townhomes for the next stage in Langley

parts.t: Langley covers two cities: the City of Langley, around the downtown core and Fraser Highway, and the much larger Township of Langley, which takes in Murrayville, Walnut Grove, Willoughby, Brookswood-Fernridge, Fort Langley and Aldergrove. Townhomes with age-restriction bylaws come up across both, so this page searches the whole Langley area.

Listings have included homes in complexes such as Chelsea Green, Chartwell Green, Orangewood, Garden Terrace and Twin Lakes. That doesn't mean every unit in those complexes shows up here, or that a given complex has an age bylaw today. The live list checks each listing's bylaw flag instead.

Many buyers here are leaving a family house in Walnut Grove, Murrayville or Brookswood and want to stay close to the same shops, church and golf course. Others are moving in from Surrey or Vancouver. Layouts range from rancher-style units with the main bedroom on the main floor to two-storey plans, so check each floor plan before you book a showing.

blocks.text: Where these townhomes are in Langley

parts.t: The City of Langley is compact. The Township borders it on the north, east and south, and Surrey is to the west. The Nicomekl River runs through the middle of the City, and its downtown core is centred on the Fraser Highway One-Way, with Glover Road heading north toward the Kwantlen Polytechnic University campus. Townhomes in the City are often a short trip from those downtown shops.

The Township is made up of separate communities, each with its own community plan. Murrayville sits on both sides of Fraser Highway, immediately east of the City. Fort Langley and Aldergrove are smaller centres with fewer townhomes, so listings there come up less often. Compare the walk to groceries, transit and a pharmacy for each complex, since that distance changes a lot between a town centre and the edge of a neighbourhood. For more on each area, see my

blocks.text: The age bylaw, in plain terms

parts.t: BC's
Strata Property Act, section 123.1

lets a strata corporation pass a bylaw that requires one or more people living in a strata lot to be at least a set age, never lower than 55. Section 123.2 lists people the bylaw doesn't apply to, such as an owner or tenant already living there when it passed, and some caregivers. Because owners can vote to change bylaws, check the current version, not an old copy.

On MLS®, the age flag is typed in by the listing agent. It won't tell you the exact age, whether the rule covers every resident, or how the strata handles visitors. Ask for the registered bylaws and the Form B before you write an offer, and I'll go through them with you.

blocks.text: Questions to ask a Langley townhome strata

parts.t: What the bylaw says.
The stated age, who it covers, and any rules for guests or a live-in caregiver.
What the fees cover.
The Form B shows the monthly fee, approved special levies and the contingency reserve fund.
What's coming up.
The depreciation report and recent minutes show planned roof, siding, fence or paving work.
Who maintains what.
Decks, patios, garage doors and small yards are split differently in each complex.
Pets, parking and RVs.
Check pet limits, visitor stalls and whether trailers or RVs are allowed.

What is a 55+ townhome in Langley?

On this page it means a townhome in Langley City or the Township whose MLS® listing is marked with an age-restriction bylaw. BC stratas can require one or more residents to be at least a set age, not lower than 55.
Are the complexes named on this page age-restricted?

Not necessarily. Listings have included homes in Chelsea Green, Chartwell Green, Orangewood, Garden Terrace and Twin Lakes, but that alone does not mean any complex is age-restricted. Bylaws can change by vote.
How do I confirm a complex's age bylaw?
Ask for the registered strata bylaws and the Form B Information Certificate, and read recent minutes. I can request these for any listing before you write an offer.
Does the bylaw apply to everyone living in the home?

It depends on the wording. A bylaw may require one resident or every resident to meet the age. Under section 123.2 of the Strata Property Act, some people are exempt, such as a resident who lived there before the bylaw passed and some caregivers.
Does this page cover both the City and the Township of Langley?
Yes. The search covers Langley City and every Township community, including Murrayville, Walnut Grove, Willoughby, Brookswood-Fernridge, Fort Langley and Aldergrove.

Yes. Most buyers on this page are also selling. Start with a free home evaluation, then call or text me at 604-928-1361 to plan the timing of both moves.
Why does the list change so often?
The listings come from MLS® and update daily. Homes sell, new ones are listed, and the age flag is entered by each listing agent, so use the live list rather than a complex name alone.
